questions.question: What specific geometric change converts the nodal-chain phase of the model crystal into the reported complete-gap phase?

options.A: Breaking inversion by making the two sphere diameters unequal gaps the nodal-line degeneracies
options.B: Increasing only the next-nearest rods removes time-reversal symmetry and gaps the valleys
options.C: Applying a magnetic field separates the six valleys without changing inversion symmetry
options.D: Removing all nearest-neighbor rods converts the nodal lines to isolated Weyl points

questions.rationale: At equal diameters inversion is retained and nodal lines occur; unequal diameters break inversion and gap them.
questions.evidence_quote: When ∆D = 0 (∆D ≡ |D1 − D2|), the inversion symmetry is preserved, and the photonic crystal hosts nodal lines along Wα± -X (α = x, y, z), forming intersecting nodal chains. The momentum of the six valleys are (±π/a, 2π/a, 0), (0, ±π/a, 2π/a), and (2π/a, 0, ±π/a) for Wx±, Wy±, and Wz±, respectively (Fig. 1(c)). When ∆D ≠ 0, however, the inversion symmetry is broken, and the nodal line degeneracies are gapped out to form a complete photonic bandgap.

questions.question: What role do the 1.2-mm next-nearest-neighbor PEC rods play in the crystal design?

options.A: They suppress high-order modes, separating the topological bands from trivial bands
options.B: They supply the inversion breaking by connecting only the larger spheres
options.C: They create the four-source phase winding needed to excite Wy valleys
options.D: They tune the external boundary condition to θV = π/2

questions.rationale: The paper adds the thinner rods to clean up the band structure rather than to impose surface termination or source chirality.
questions.evidence_quote: Each nearest sphere is connected by PEC rods with diameter B1 = 2.4 mm. Additionally, we connect the next-nearest spheres by PEC rods with diameter B2 = 1.2 mm to suppress high-order modes, so that we can obtain a clean bandstructure where the topological bands are separated from the trivial bands [21].

questions.question: How is the valley-pair distinction encoded in the local effective Hamiltonian?

options.A: The valley sign multiplies the two transverse momentum terms, while the inversion-breaking mass is m=(ω1−ω2)/2
options.B: The valley sign multiplies only the scalar mass, which equals the lattice constant
options.C: Each pair is described by a scalar Dirac model with no momentum-dependent Pauli terms
options.D: The mass is set by the difference in rod diameters and is independent of inversion

questions.rationale: The k·p model assigns valley-dependent signs to the two momentum terms and identifies the frequency splitting as the mass.
questions.evidence_quote: where (α, β, γ) = (x, y, z), (y, z, x), or (z, x, y), q = (qx, qy, qz) represents the momentum offset from each valley, vD is the group velocity, σx,y,z are Pauli matrices, and m = (ω1 − ω2)/2 is the mass term induced by breaking the inversion symmetry, with ω1,2 the angular frequencies of the two bands at the valleys [21].

questions.question: In the Wy experiment at 13.8 GHz, which source phase winding selects Wy− and what direction is measured?

options.A: (0, π/2, π, 3π/2) selects Wy− and outcouples at −32.9°
options.C: Equal phases select Wy− and outcouple at 0°
options.D: (0, π, 0, π) selects Wy− and outcouples at −90°

questions.rationale: The clockwise winding is assigned to Wy−, whose measured direction is the negative angle; the opposite winding selects Wy+.
questions.evidence_quote: Taking valley states at Wy± as an example, the relative phase delay of each source is set to (0, π/2, π, 3π/2) for Wy− and (0, −π/2, −π, −3π/2) for Wy+, to form a clockwise or counterclockwise phase winding in the x-z plane (see Fig. 2(a)). The excited valley states will outcouple to the free space radiation and, thus, the momentum of the excited valley state can be judged from the outcoupling direction (see Figs. 2(b) and (c)). As shown in Fig. 2(d), the measured outcoupling fields at 13.8 GHz exhibit different directions: for the clockwise (counterclockwise) phase winding, the direction is −32.9° (+32.9°), corresponding to Wy− (Wy+) , while for the case without phase winding, the direction is 0°, corresponding to X, since the states at X coexist with valley states at the same frequency [22].

questions.question: What vectorial Chern assignments do the authors calculate for the three valley pairs?

options.B: Every valley carries the same scalar value +1/2 in all three directions
options.D: Each pair has zero Chern vector because time reversal forces all components to vanish

questions.rationale: The nonzero component is aligned with the distinct directional valley pair, and its sign changes between ± valleys.
questions.evidence_quote: We calculate the valley Chern vector (VCV) [Cv = (Cvx, Cvy, Cvz)], which is (±1/2, 0, 0), (0, ±1/2, 0), and (0, 0, ±1/2) for Wx±, Wy±, and Wz± valleys, respectively [21].

questions.question: What boundary tuning did the authors use to realize the chiral surface-state boundary condition on the (001) surface?

options.A: They chose θV=π/2 and used a metallic plate with h=6.25 mm and D3=4 mm
options.B: They chose θV=0 and used h=4 mm and D3=6.25 mm
options.C: They created an opposite-valley domain wall and removed the plate
options.D: They set h=a/2 and D3 equal to the larger bulk sphere diameter

questions.rationale: The derivation requires θV=π/2; the experimental termination was obtained by tuning the plate gap and outer-sphere diameter to the stated values.
questions.evidence_quote:
We find that when h = 6.25 mm and
D3 = 4 mm, the boundary condition can be satisfied [21].

questions.question: Which observation did the authors use as experimental evidence for surface states in the bulk gap?

options.A: Surface transmission remained high while bulk transmission was substantially lower
options.B: Both surface and bulk transmission vanished across the complete gap
options.C: The bulk transmission exceeded surface transmission at every gap frequency
options.D: The surface mode appeared only outside the bulk gap and had a flat dispersion

questions.rationale: High transmission confined to the surface together with lower bulk transmission is the reported signature of the gap-spanning surface channel.
questions.evidence_quote: The measured surface transmission, depicted in Fig. 3(e), maintains high within the complete photonic bandgap, while the bulk transmission is substantially lower, which verifies the existence of the surface states. We also map out the surface field distribution (Fig. 3(f)) and obtain its Fourier-transformed spectrum along L4- Wx−-L1 (Fig. 3(g)). We can indeed observe a nearly-linear surface dispersion in the bandgap.

questions.question: What physical feature explains the reported diffractionless propagation of the surface state?

options.A: Its flat isofrequency contour preserves group velocity as transverse wavevector varies
options.B: A large density of bulk states traps the wave at the surface
options.C: The measured state repeatedly scatters between opposite valleys
options.D: A quadratic dispersion makes the group velocity vanish at all transverse momenta

questions.rationale: The paper attributes canalization to flat contours and notes that the dispersion is independent of the wavevector transverse to propagation.
questions.evidence_quote: Note that the chiral surface states exhibit canalization behaviour; that is, the surface states propagate diffractionlessly along the +y direction, corresponding to the Wx− valley. This canalization phenomenon is due to the flat isofrequancy contour of the surface states, which has been confirmed both experimentally and numerically (Fig. 3(h)) [25–27]. The canalization has previously been explored at the topological transition point between open hyperbolic and closed elliptical isofrequency contours, as in the twisted van der Waals bilayers [26]. From the equation of the surface states aforementioned, one can see that the surface dispersion is independent of the wavevector vertical to the propagation direction (denoted as kx (ky)), indicating that the group velocity of surface states preserves for different ky (kx) around each valley, which leads to the flat isofrequency contours.

questions.question: For a Wx− state crossing from the (001) to (010) face, what path and robustness did the experiment report?

options.A: It travels +y then −z and passes the sharp corner with high transmission without intervalley scattering
options.B: It travels −y then +z but is reflected at the corner by intervalley scattering
options.C: It remains on the (001) face because its valley has no projection on (010)
options.D: It travels +z then +y and requires a bulk mode to cross the bend

questions.rationale: The measured surface channel follows the valley-locked direction around the corner while maintaining high transmission.
questions.evidence_quote: The excited surface states propagate along the +y direction, corresponding to Wx− valley. Owing to the valley conservation, the surface states smoothly pass through the sharp corner with high transmission (see Fig. 4(c)) and propagate along the −z direction. We also perform Fourier transform on the field distributions on the (001) and (010) surfaces, respectively.

questions.question: What limitation of earlier 3D topological photonic insulators motivates the all-surface geometry claimed here?

options.A: Their topological surface states were restricted to certain faces, whereas this valley crystal can host them on every sample surface
options.B: They had no time-reversal symmetry and therefore no valleys
options.C: They required optical rather than microwave frequencies
options.D: Their states were confined to domain walls and could not be measured

questions.rationale: The authors contrast face-restricted states of earlier systems with their shape supporting chiral valley states on all three orthogonal surface orientations.
questions.evidence_quote: Unlike the existing 3D topological photonic insulators [29–34] in which the topological surface states can only exist on certain surfaces, the 3D VPCs with certain shapes can support the chiral valley surface states on all sample surfaces. Obviously, our fabricated sample can support the chiral valley surface states on all (100), (010), and (001) surfaces, with the propagation direction locked to each valley.
